name: Dial
description: An invitee-first, self-hosted scheduler for one business or independent host.
nonGoals: Group events, classes, waitlists, or resource capacity
Additional invitee guests on a booking
Bookings that wait for host approval before they are confirmed
Payments, deposits, refunds, or booking fees
Recurring booking series or scheduling polls
Marketplace discovery, ratings, or invitee-submitted reviews
SMS, WhatsApp, phone automation, CRM, campaigns, or marketing automation
Automatic adoption of arbitrary external-calendar time or location edits

externals.why: A connected calendar supplies busy-time checks and destination events. An explicitly not_connected host can still publish from saved availability with a non-Meet location; a configured but unhealthy connection remains fail-closed, and Google Meet requires a healthy conference-capable calendar. The maintained setup journey covers the calendar-optional case at 1440 and 390 pixels.

The prototype's default location is a real Google Meet conference, which requires provider-side conference creation. EVENT-004 also lets an event type use a fixed link, a phone number, or an in-person address instead, so a deployment can run with no event type ever using Meet.
Managed hosting supplies the mail.sender.v1 relay and installation credential. Direct provider credentials are not needed on Managed. No fallback is selected if the configured provider fails.

Direct installs select SendGrid through mail.sender.v1 for sign-in and transactional messages. Managed installs use the RER relay instead. EVENT-006 blocks publication while the selected mail connection is unhealthy.

Existing installations may retain their Resend credentials and mail.sender.v1 configuration. New setup selects SendGrid; an explicitly configured provider failure is not replaced with another provider.

env.name: ENVIRONMENT
env.why: Deployment mode: development, preview, or production. Controls local magic-link sink availability and cookie transport security.

env.name: APP_URL
env.why: Canonical deployment origin used in public links; local development uses its loopback HTTP origin.

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.why: Hashes opaque operator session and magic-link tokens.

env.name: OWNER_EMAIL
env.why: The setup-supplied identity of the first operator. The operator-auth store persists this identity explicitly and does not create or select a fixture operator.

env.name: SETUP_TOKEN
env.why: One-use credential for first-operator bootstrap on an empty auth store. Its durable bootstrap ledger rejects reuse; this bootstrap is independent of mail.sender.v1 and creates no fixture operator.

env.name: MAIL_PROVIDER
env.why: Selects the explicit RER Managed relay, SendGrid, retained Resend, or loopback-development mail.sender.v1 provider. Missing or unhealthy mail blocks publication.

env.name: MAIL_API_KEY
env.why: Authenticates the selected mail.sender.v1 provider. Missing or invalid credentials fail the provider connection check and block normal or request-only publication.

env.name: MAIL_FROM
env.why: Verified sender for the selected mail.sender.v1 provider; Managed hosting assigns it.

env.name: MAIL_RELAY_URL
env.why: HTTPS relay endpoint for the RER Managed mail.sender.v1 adapter, supplied by Managed hosting.

env.name: MAIL_WEBHOOK_KEY
env.why: Optional mail.sender.v1 SendGrid Event Webhook ECDSA P-256 public verification key for authenticated bounce callbacks. Absent means delivery and bounce tracking is off; unsigned callbacks remain rejected. Sender verification and event publication require the API key and verified sender, not this optional tracking key. Opt in to its deploy declaration and use rer deploy --set-secret to enable signed callback processing.

env.name: RESEND_API_KEY
env.why: Legacy Resend credential retained for installed mail.sender.v1 compatibility. If selected, its connection must pass before event publication.

env.name: RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
env.why: Verified no-reply sender used by the mail.sender.v1 adapter for magic links and transactional messages.

env.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env.why: Identifies the calendar.provider.v2 Google OAuth client. Without OAuth client configuration, the host cannot connect Google Calendar; an explicitly not_connected host can still publish from saved availability with a non-Meet location. A configured but unhealthy connection remains fail-closed; live OAuth acceptance is separate.

env.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
env.why: Authenticates the calendar.provider.v2 Google OAuth client during authorisation and token refresh. Missing OAuth credentials prevent a healthy connected-calendar setup; explicit not_connected publication remains available from saved availability with a non-Meet location, while a configured but unhealthy connection fails closed. Google Meet requires a healthy conference-capable calendar.

env.name: CALENDAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.why: Authenticates calendar.provider.v2 push callbacks when a Google Calendar is connected. Without it, callbacks are rejected and connected-calendar health checks cannot succeed; this does not block the explicit not_connected saved-availability/non-Meet publication path. Live callback behavior requires separate acceptance.

env.name: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.why: Authenticates mail.sender.v1 Resend delivery and bounce callback signatures.

env.name: IDENTITY_PROVIDER
env.why: Optional Auth installation URL for the oidc-provider@1 setup dependency. Empty keeps email-link sign-in through mail.sender.v1.

operatingCost.basis: One host and operator, 1,000 unchanged bookings per month, four to six transactional emails per booking including the default reminders when both offsets apply (4,000–6,000 sends/month), with Google Calendar and Cloudflare usage inside the stated allowances.
operatingCost.notes: Twilio SendGrid Essentials 50k was $19.95/month on 2026-10-14; 4,000–6,000 sends use 8–12% of its 50,000 monthly allowance. The low estimate assumes the full Cloudflare runtime fits available free allowances. The typical estimate adds $5/month for Cloudflare Workers Paid, conditional on all metered use staying within included allowances; an owner already paying for that Cloudflare account may incur no additional $5 for Dial. Google Calendar standard use and first-tier R2 usage are assumed within their published free allowances. Estimates exclude overages, domains, taxes, optional tools and paid Google Workspace. The SendGrid trial is limited to 60 days and 100 emails/day, so it is not recurring free service. Extra operators, sign-ins, requests, changes, late Meet links, retries and alerts increase mail volume.
